- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly below recent highs, adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is above recent lows, adjust downward by 1–2% to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0) and price is trending, apply slight lag correction: forecast 1–2 days behind actual trend direction.  
- For 30-day horizons, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, reweight forecast toward recent 7-day average to reduce overfitting.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.0 values, assume low volatility; cap forecast range within ±2% of recent 14-day mean.
